title: Applied ML Evals: Cross-Functional Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the cross-functional standards and operational playbooks for Applied ML evaluation at Redwood Inference. It brings together guidance for the eval-harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage. The objective is to ensure consistent, reproducible evaluation and fast, reliable triage when quality regressions occur.

Intended audience
- ML engineers and researchers
- Platform and runtime engineers
- Product managers and SREs involved in model rollouts

Goals
- Provide a single reference for evaluation artifacts and processes.
- Define SLOs and thresholds used for automated monitoring and alerts.
- Standardize model onboarding and rollback criteria.
- Reduce mean time to detect and remediate regressions.

Scope
- Applies to all models served through Redwood: hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Covers offline evals (eval-harness), continuous monitoring (quality-monitor), and manual regression triage.

Roles and ownership
- Applied ML (owner): maintains prompt sets, eval harness configs, and primary triage lead.
- Serving Runtime (owner): provides perf profiles, kernel/quantization guidance, and latency budgets.
- Eng-SRE: integrates alerts into incident pipelines and manages infra for evaluators.
- Product: approves gating thresholds for feature rollouts.

Key services and artifacts
- eval-harness-service: primary CI/CD runner for offline evals; stores results in s3://redwood-evals (versioned).
- quality-monitor: streaming metric processor that computes running evals on production traces and synthetic probe traffic.
- prompt-set-catalog: curated prompt sets with metadata (language, dialect, prompt-intent, tags).
- quant-profiles registry: named quantization profiles (q8_2, q4_0, q5_1) with expected perf/accuracy tradeoffs.

Standards and Playbooks

1) Eval Harness (offline)

Purpose: reproducible, CI-driven regression detection and model comparison.

Required artifacts per model version:
- canonical eval config (YAML) stored under eval-configs/<model-name>/<version>.yaml
- baseline checkpoint id and commit hash
- prompt sets referenced by id (prompt-set-ids)
- metric definitions (JSON schema)

Minimum CI checks (when a new model or quantization profile is introduced):
1. Unit coverage: run fast smoke tests against 10 representative prompts (max 3s end-to-end).
2. Regression suite: run full prompt set (target 5k examples) and compute primary metrics (accuracy/EM, hallucination rate, formatting error rate).
3. Performance profiling: measure p50/p95 latency and peak memory for typical sequence lengths (64/512/2048 tokens).

Example eval-config snippet (YAML as text):
---
model: redwood-chat-13b
prompt_sets: [dialogue-safety-v2, qa-base-2026]
metrics: [exact_match, rouge_l, hallucination_rate]
quant_profile: q8_2
---

Acceptance criteria (CI gate):
- No regression > 2.0% absolute on primary metric vs baseline OR
- If regression 2.0%-5.0%, require sign-off from Applied ML + Product with documented justification.
- Regressions > 5.0% are auto-blocking and trigger regression triage (see section below).

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

Catalog requirements: every prompt set MUST include:
- id, owner, creation_date, domain tags, language, expected-label-format
- provenance notes (source, synthetic/real, licensing)
- target coverage (intent distribution, difficulty levels)

Benchmarking cadence:
- Core benchmarks (safety, factuality, formatting) run weekly on mainline models.
- Customer-privacy-sensitive prompts live in restricted prompt sets (confidentiality: restricted) and are only used in private deployments with proper access controls.

Prompt-set curation process (high level):
1. Submit request to prompt-set-catalog with rationale and representative examples.
2. Applied ML reviews and assigns tags and target metrics.
3. QA-runner executes integration smoke tests; if OK, set status=published.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (summary)

Required pre-onboarding checklist:
- Training artifact provenance + license check.
- Baseline eval run against canonical prompt sets.
- Cost and latency estimate from serving-runtime: expected p50 and p95 for target sequence lengths.
- Quantization compatibility matrix: which quant profiles are supported.
- Security review (if model trains on customer data).

Onboarding steps (numbered):
1. Create model onboarding ticket in JIRA with required artifacts linked.
2. Run eval-harness CI suite and attach results to ticket.
3. Run perf profile on staging deployment (use redwood-load-test tool).
4. Stakeholder review: Applied ML, Serving Runtime, Eng-SRE, Product.
5. Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 24 hours with quality-monitor probes enabled.
6. If metrics stable, increase to 10% for 48 hours and then full rollout.

Rollback criteria (automatic):
- Any primary metric regression > 5.0% sustained for 30 minutes.
- Hallucination rate spike to > 3x baseline and absolute > 2.0% for 15 minutes.
- Latency p95 > 2x expected budget for 30 minutes.

4) Quality Guardrails

Guardrail types:
- Structural checks: output JSON schema validation, token-length limits, enforced tool-calling safety.
- Safety filters: blacklist heuristics + ML-based safety scorer (safety-score < 0.6 triggers block).
- Factuality probes: retrieval-based checks with thresholded similarity.

Operational thresholds (examples):
- Output schema validation failure rate should be < 0.5% per 24h window.
- Safety-score: > 0.7 baseline target; scores < 0.6 send to human-review queue.

Implementation notes:
- Guardrails executed in redwood-runtime as a post-processing pipeline stage; config lives in guardrails/configs/<model>.yaml.
- For private deployments, guardrails are configurable per-customer with recommended defaults.

5) Quantization Profiles

Registry entries must include:
- profile_id (e.g. q8_2), supported hardware (A100, H100, T4), expected accuracy delta vs fp16, expected latency improvements.

Recommended profiles (examples):
| profile_id | target_latency_p50 | expected_accuracy_delta | recommended_use_cases |
|------------|--------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------|
| q8_2      | p50 < 40ms (64 tokens) | -1.2% abs on EM         | dev, low-cost hosted  |
| q5_1      | p50 < 30ms (64 tokens) | -3.5% abs on EM         | high-throughput internal |
| q4_0      | p50 < 25ms (64 tokens) | -6.0% abs on EM         | experimental, extreme cost-savings |

Quantization rollout guidance:
1. Evaluate accuracy delta on canonical eval sets (must be < 3.0% absolute on primary metric for production use).
2. Run perf profile on target hardware.
3. If accuracy delta within threshold, include profile in canary for 3 days and monitor quality-monitor.
4. Document customer-facing consequences in the model card.

6) Regression Triage Playbook

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- Automated regression alert when: drop in primary metric >= 2.0% absolute over baseline AND p-value < 0.05 for effect size.
- Critical alert when: drop >= 5.0% or hallucination rate >= 3x baseline AND absolute > 2.0%.

Triage steps (ordered):
1. Pager triggers Applied ML on-call and creates triage incident in Incident Bot.
2. Initial checklist (10 minutes): confirm alert validity, check eval-harness results for recent changes, review recent deploys and quant-profile changes.
3. If caused by code/config change: assign to Serving Runtime for rollback or patch.
4. If caused by model weights or data drift: assign to Applied ML for model rollback and re-eval.
5. Mitigation: temporary routing policy (route to fallback model variant) or rate-limiting (reduce user traffic to affected route).
6. Postmortem: within 3 business days, document root cause, impact, and remediation steps.

Triage checklist (quick):
- Recent commits to model or eval configs? (git SHA)
- New quantization profile applied?
- Infrastructure anomalies (GPU OOM, kernel fallback)
- Input distribution shift (compare production vs canonical prompt distributions)

Reporting and metrics
- Dashboards: per-model quality dashboard (primary metric, hallucination, schema-failure rate, latency p50/p95).
- Key SLOs: primary-metric stability (no >2% daily regression), guardrail-failure rate <1% per 24h, rolling false-positive rate for safety <5%.

Example CLI commands
- Run a smoke eval locally: redwood-eval run --config eval-configs/redwood-chat-13b/smoke.yaml --out results/smoke.json
- Compare two results: redwood-eval diff results/baseline.json results/new.json --metrics exact_match, hallucination_rate

Maintenance and cadence
- Weekly: core benchmarks for mainline models.
- Monthly: review and prune prompt sets, update quantization profiles with new hardware data.
- Quarterly: cross-functional audit (Applied ML, Serving Runtime, Eng-SRE, Product) to review gating thresholds and incident history.

Appendix: Glossary and links
- model-card: model cards stored at /docs/model-cards/<model-name>.md
- eval-harness CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/eval-harness (internal)
- incident playbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: Applied ML on-call (pager team: applied-ml-oncall).
- For urgent infra issues, alert Eng-SRE pager.

This document is intended to be the canonical cross-functional reference. For component-level procedures (deep dive into eval-harness internals or quantization kernel tuning), see the linked pages in related_pages.
